text.p: Arsenal striker Ian Wright's hopes of escaping punishment for his dismissal at Nottingham Forest a week ago have been dashed by referee Stephen Lodge, the Football Association said on Saturday.

Lodge has decided not to revise his decision to dismiss Wright for an off-the-ball clash with Nikola Jerkan, even though manager Arsene Wenger tagged the Croat defender "a cheat" after watching video re-runs of the incident.
Referee Lodge studied the same tapes and his view is that Wright, who has 21 goals this season, deserved to go.
He will now be ruled out for three games, which could turn into five if he collects another booking to take him over the disciplinary threshhold.
The Football Association announced on Saturday: "Ian Wright's three match suspension following his sending off at Nottingham Forest last Saturday will go ahead in the New Year.
"Over the Christmas holiday referee Stephen Lodge, and his assistant John Holbrook, both watched a video of the relevant incident from the game at the City Ground.
"They have stood by their original view that the incident _ involving Wright and Forest's Nikola Jerkan _ merited a sending off. Ian Wright's suspension begins on January 4."
That will rule him out of the F.A. Cup tie against Sunderland and his loss is a big blow to second-placed Arsenal's title push.
Wright clashed with Jerkan after the Forest man had been penalised for a blatant obstruction.
"It is obvious from the video that Jerkan was cheating," said Wenger. "I agree Ian Wright might have acted provocatively but the reaction of Jerkan was ridiculous."
Sendings off can only be quashed if the referee is prepared to change his mind. The F.A. have no option but to back his decision.
